<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Follow existing conventions; check sibling files when creating/editing files. MUST activate the relevant skill whenever you work in that domain—don't wait until you're stuck.

`wayfinder-development` activates whenever referencing backend routes in frontend components, including `@/actions`, `@/routes`, Laravel routes from TypeScript, or Wayfinder route functions.
`pest-testing` activates when writing/debugging tests, assertions, datasets, mocks, browser/Livewire tests, or when the user mentions test, spec, TDD, expects, assertion, coverage, or verification.

Use descriptive variable/method names and reusable components. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise.

Use Laravel Boost MCP tools. Use `list-artisan-commands` before Artisan commands when checking parameters. Use `get-absolute-url` for every project URL. Use `tinker` for PHP/Eloquent debugging; `database-query` for read-only database access; `database-schema` before migrations/models; `browser-logs` for recent browser logs only; `search-docs` before version-specific code changes, using multiple broad simple queries and package arrays when known. Do not add package names to search queries.

Always use curly braces for control structures. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion. Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless the constructor is private. Always use explicit return type declarations and appropriate parameter type hints. Prefer PHPDoc blocks. Never use comments within the code itself unless the logic is exceptionally complex.

The app is served by Laravel Herd at `https?://[kebab-case-project-dir].test`; use `get-absolute-url` for valid URLs. You must not run any commands to make the site available via HTTP(S). It is always available through Laravel Herd.

Every change must be programmatically tested. Write a new test or update an existing test, then run affected tests. Run the minimum: `php artisan test --compact` with a specific filename or filter.

If frontend changes are not reflected, ask the user to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`.

Use `Inertia::render()` instead of Blade views. ALWAYS use `search-docs` for version-specific Inertia documentation. Deferred props require an empty pulsing or animated skeleton.

Use `php artisan make:` to create files; generic PHP classes use `php artisan make:class`. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands and correct `--options`. Use typed Eloquent relationships, `Model::query()`, eager loading, Form Requests, named routes, queued jobs with `ShouldQueue`, and `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. Never use the `env()` function directly outside of config files.

For tests use `php artisan make:test [options] {name}`; pass `--unit` for unit tests; most should be feature tests. CRITICAL: ALWAYS use `search-docs` for version-specific Laravel documentation.

Import Wayfinder routes from `@/actions/` or `@/routes/`. IMPORTANT: Activate `wayfinder-development` skill whenever referencing backend routes in frontend components.
</laravel-boost-guidelines>
